title: Fleet writes as `objectstack-fleet[bot]` from cloud seats: a `repository_dispatch` relay workflow in objectstack + a `dispatch` transport in the five PM write tools (maintainer direct dispatch, 「方案 1」)
body:
③ 直派任务 — maintainer direct dispatch, filed by the director seat (summon #27, `session_0129ZpnaBcYZZ51rCvQiXg6C`). `domain:skills` · `tooling` · dispatched from this seat under the maintainer's words; ⛔ not a queue card.

**Provenance (who / verbatim / where):** the maintainer, in chat with the director seat, 2026-09-22 — 「我首先要解决的问题是车队怎么用 github app 的身份跑,所以还有什么可用的方案」 · 「方案 1,先发探针」 · 「车队不只是在这两个仓库,objectstack-ai 组织下的所有仓库都可能会用」 · 「OS_FLEET_ALLOWED_SENDERS 听下来不需要,首先需要有 objectstack 仓库权限才能调用对吧」 · 「为什么需要这个,每个用车队的仓放一个桩 fleet-write.yml,每个用车队的仓我在开启云会话时都会加入objectstack 仓库」 · 「你现在就派发处理」 · 「OS_FLEET_PRIVATE_KEY 已经改为组织 secret」.

## The measured problem

Cloud seat containers cannot act as the fleet App `objectstack-fleet` (App id `5028251`, installation `163654544`, bot user `objectstack-fleet[bot]`). Readings taken by the director seat on 2026-09-22 between 08:46Z and 09:04Z, all through the session proxy:

- `POST /app/installations/163654544/access_tokens`, `GET /app`, `GET /app/installations/163654544` → HTTP 403 「Access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy」. The proxy passes repo-scoped paths and `/rate_limit` only.
- The proxy REPLACES any caller-supplied `Authorization` header: `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack` with `Authorization: Bearer garbage-not-a-token` → 200, `GET /user` with the same header → `os-support-ai`. ⇒ a minted App token could not be used from a cloud container even if one existed.
- `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/variables` and `/actions/secrets` → 403 (the token minter's second input route is dead in cloud containers too).
- Arbitrary egress: example.com, api.cloudflare.com, httpbin.org → CONNECT 403. An external broker is unreachable without an environment policy change.
- What passes: `POST /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/dispatches` with `event_type: fleet-probe` → **204** at 09:04Z (zero listeners on `repository_dispatch` in the tree, zero runs afterwards). The session token's repo permission: `push: true`.

Industry check (director seat, same day): GitHub's own guidance is App over machine user, with `actions/create-github-app-token` as the in-Actions pattern; Devin and Claude Code cloud attribute to a product App whose key the sandbox never holds; agentbox / agent-bot-identity mint per request behind a broker with default-deny per repo and operation. Same pattern; GitHub Actions is the broker a cloud seat can reach.

## Ruled shape — ⛔ not open for re-design; the forks were closed in chat

Two PRs, both in objectstack, both `Part of` this card (⛔ neither carries `Fixes`; the director closes the card after the live probe).

### PR A — the relay: `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml` + `scripts/pm/fleet-write/`

1. **Trigger**: `repository_dispatch` with `types: [fleet-write]` only; no other trigger. `permissions: {}` for the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` — the run's only write path is the App token of step 5. `run-name: fleet-write <request_id>` so a seat finds its run by name.
2. **Payload, closed schema** (validator `scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs`, hand-written, no dependency, shared verbatim by the seat tools' packer): `{ request_id: string ≤ 64, repo: "objectstack-ai/<name>", session: "session_…", actions: [ 1..20 ] }`. Unknown top-level or per-action keys ⇒ refuse. Per-op required keys, integer numbers, string caps (comment/body ≤ 60000 bytes, title ≤ 256). A refusal fails the run at the validate step with zero writes and the reason in the step summary. Measure and pin GitHub's `client_payload` limits (top-level property count and byte size) in the validator's self-test.
3. **Sender gate** (the maintainer's ruling: no sender allowlist variable — GitHub's write permission on the TARGET repo is the authorization): `github.event.sender.login` is what GitHub filled from the dispatching token. After the App token exists, the executor calls `GET /repos/{payload.repo}/collaborators/{sender}/permission` and refuses unless `permission` ∈ {`write`, `maintain`, `admin`}. Refusal = run failure, zero writes. This is what carries the authorization from objectstack (where every dispatch lands) to the target repo.
4. **Target repo**: `payload.repo`, any repository of the `objectstack-ai` organization the App is installed on; the workflow never writes to a repo the payload did not name.
5. **App token**: `actions/create-github-app-token@v2` with `app-id: ${{ vars.OS_FLEET_APP_ID }}`, `private-key: ${{ secrets.OS_FLEET_PRIVATE_KEY }}` (organization secret, set by the maintainer 2026-09-22), `owner: objectstack-ai`, `repositories: <payload.repo name>`, and the `permission-*` inputs narrowed to what the action set needs (measure: `issues: write`, `pull-requests: write`, and whatever the permission read of step 3 requires; declare only those). The token is used only inside the executor step and revoked by the action's post step.
6. **Executor** `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` (node, no dependency): runs the actions in order against `api.github.com` with the App token; stops at the first failure (later actions not attempted); writes a `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` table — request_id · sender · session · target · per action: op, endpoint, HTTP status, resulting id / url. Text is passed through unchanged: attribution stays the session ID inside the text, per protocol.
7. **Closed op list, v1**: `comment` (POST /issues/{n}/comments) · `comment_edit` (PATCH /issues/comments/{id}) · `labels_add` (POST /issues/{n}/labels) · `labels_remove` (DELETE /issues/{n}/labels/{name}, one per name) · `assign` / `unassign` (POST / DELETE /issues/{n}/assignees) · `issue_patch` (PATCH /issues/{n}: `title`, `body`, `state`, `state_reason` only) · `issue_create` (POST /issues: title, body, labels, assignees) · `pr_create` (POST /pulls, `draft: true` forced) · `pr_request_reviewers` (POST /pulls/{n}/requested_reviewers) · `pr_ready` / `pr_draft` (GraphQL `markPullRequestReadyForReview` / `convertPullRequestToDraft`) · `automerge_enable` / `automerge_disable` (GraphQL `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` with `SQUASH` / `disablePullRequestAutoMerge`). ⛔ Refused by the validator, by construction: merge, any review submission, branch or ref writes, contents or workflow writes, releases, org or admin endpoints.
8. **Self-tests**: `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/validate.mjs --self-test` and `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs --self-test` (fake platform, no network — the pattern of `scripts/pm/fleet-token.mjs --self-test`), wired into `package.json` `check:*` the way `check:pm-post-stamped` is.
9. **Landing**: `.github/workflows/**` — the maintainer merges by hand (seat tokens cannot land workflow changes); `skip-changeset`; PR body carries the verification record and the live-probe plan below.

### PR B — the seats' side: a `dispatch` transport in the five write tools

`scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs`, `label-write.mjs`, `issue-create.mjs`, `close-cards.mjs`, `with-fleet.sh` (shell entry `--via dispatch`).

1. **Selection**: env `OS_FLEET_TRANSPORT` ∈ `direct | dispatch | auto`, default `auto`: `dispatch` when the process runs in a cloud seat container (measure the discriminator; the `CCR_*` environment family is the candidate; ⛔ do not key on the proxy port), else `direct`.
2. **One stroke = one dispatch**: each tool packs the SAME requests it would have sent directly into ONE payload (label-write's adds + removes + assignee change travel together; post-stamped's one comment or one body), POSTs `/repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/dispatches` with the session token (always the board repo; `payload.repo` names the target), polls `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs?event=repository_dispatch&per_page=20` for the run whose name carries the `request_id`, waits for its `conclusion`, then performs the tool's existing read-back against the target object unchanged (post-stamped's read-back, label-write's step ④). Measure run start latency and set a ceiling (≈ 5 min); on ceiling exit non-zero with `UNCONFIRMED` + the run URL — ⛔ never silent, ⛔ never auto-retried (a retry would double-write).
3. **Stamps**: post-stamped substitutes `NOW` / `WAS` tokens before packing (the stamp is the seat's act). `write-pace` counts the dispatch as the write; budget and gap unchanged.
4. **Four-step label write keeps its shape**: ① read current set (direct GET — reads are unaffected), ② compute, ③ dispatch the additive verbs, ④ read back. The whole-set PATCH fallback is ⛔ not carried into the dispatch transport; the executor only has additive verbs.
5. **Inert until A is live**: when the dispatch returns the status a repo without the listening workflow returns (measure it; a 204 with no run is the likely shape — then the run-poller's ceiling is what detects it), `auto` prints one line and falls back to `direct`; ⛔ never silent.
6. **Self-tests** for the packer and the run-poller (fake platform); every existing self-test stays green. `scripts/pm/**` is not on the governed register — ordinary queue landing after the seat's review; PR B may land before PR A.

## Maintainer's actions (prerequisites for the live probe, ⛔ not for the code)

1. ✅ Organization secret `OS_FLEET_PRIVATE_KEY` — done 2026-09-22 (「OS_FLEET_PRIVATE_KEY 已经改为组织 secret」).
2. Organization variable `OS_FLEET_APP_ID` = `5028251` (not a secret), visible to objectstack.
3. App `objectstack-fleet` → repository access **All repositories**.

After PR A lands and 2–3 exist: the director seat sends one live `fleet-write` with a `comment` action on this card and reads back `user.login == objectstack-fleet[bot]`; then closes the card.
